claims.statement: The lcchess console script maps to langchain_chess_cli.main:app, a Typer app with uci, play and grade subcommands; the CLI requires Python >=3.13 and offers an optional anthropic extra.

The CLI is installed without cloning via uv from the git subdirectory libs/cli (uvx or uv tool install) because the packages are not on PyPI and uv resolves sibling packages from the same commit; an installed lcchess doesn't read .env, and calling Anthropic directly with a bare model name needs the anthropic extra plus LANGSMITH_GATEWAY unset.
mise run dev:tui runs `uv run --all-packages --env-file .env lcchess play`, with extra play options passed after `--`.

play and uci expose one flag per ChessContext setting, built by _setting from the field's description and default; every flag defaults to None so an omitted flag keeps the base settings' value, and defaults come from ChessContext settings version 3 (policy hybrid, model langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, reasoning_effort unset, model_kwargs {}, show_fen/show_board on, move_list both, memory off, systemone_model typesafe/jev-latest, threshold 0.9, k 5, gate margin, style rich, seed 0); play additionally takes --side, --fen and --draw-claims.

The CLI uses the shared langchain_chess_systemone.agent.build_agent, which adds SystemOneMiddleware for every policy except llm; for policy systemone it never calls the model factory and configures System 1 with threshold and tournament_threshold 0.0 and has_model=False, so System 1 always plays.

build_agent enables memory only when settings.memory is set and a model exists (so it is dropped for policy systemone); with memory on and a model whose input_limit is None it raises ChessContractError saying the model has no known input limit, so it can't use memory.

The default model is chat_model(settings.model, arguments(settings)), with model_kwargs merged over reasoning_effort; chat_model rejects a reasoning effort for a model that doesn't take one and a max_tokens that fills the window (ModelArgumentsError, a ValueError), sets an output budget of MAX_TOKENS 64000 capped by the model's output limit and half of a smaller window, names the span after the bare model name, sends a reasoning effort only when set, and gives langsmith: gateway models with a known window a profile with max_input_tokens = window minus the budget.

run_config(surface, thread_id, settings) sets configurable.thread_id, run_name chess-<surface>, tags [surface], and metadata with the surface, every settings key from dump(settings) (including version and draw_claims), overlaid by sent(settings) so reasoning_effort (and max_tokens when set) record the values actually sent after model_kwargs; the TUI calls it with surface tui and the current game's context, and the UCI engine with surface uci.

play and uci both pass a factory(settings, checkpointer) that calls build_agent(settings, checkpointer=...); play's draw claims follow settings.draw_claims while the UCI engine forces draw_claims never. ChessApp creates its own InMemorySaver and calls the factory in its constructor for the first Game, so TUI games are not persisted beyond the process and a ValueError from building (e.g. an effort the model can't take) becomes typer.BadParameter with exit code 2 before the TUI opens.

ChessApp binds ctrl+n (New Game screen), ctrl+s (start), ctrl+r (retry), ctrl+f (flip the board), ctrl+g (resign), ctrl+o (offer draw), comma/full stop (step back/forward), home/end (first move/live) and ctrl+q (quit); check_action hides start, retry, resign and offer draw from the footer when they can't apply.

The TUI keeps no board of its own: it rebuilds boards by replaying the thread's moves from start_fen (positions, board_at) and renders strips, move list, result and Last Reply from pure view, reply and setup functions over the thread state; before a turn accepts a custom root, the root comes from the game's start FEN.

Moves can be entered by clicking a piece then a target, by arrow keys plus Enter/Space on the board, or by typing SAN/UCI into the input; keys pressed on the board that can start a move or go (abcdefghKQRBNO0) are forwarded to the input via a Typed message unless the input is disabled, and board moves arrive as Moved(uci) messages that go through the same _play path as typed text.

The TUI parses typed text locally with parse_chat on the latest board: go, resign <side> and draw <side> run the same actions as their keys (for the human's side whatever side was typed, with a notice when they can't apply), a parse error's CommandError text is shown in the #note line, and rejections the agent records in the thread's error field show as 'Move rejected: ...'.

The board widget only accepts selection when interactive (otherwise it rings the bell), clears the selection when the position changes or it becomes non-interactive, and opens a PromotionScreen for promotions where the chosen letter is appended to the UCI and cancel posts nothing.

Board geometry picks the largest square height that fits with square width 2*h+1 and supports both orientations for drawing and click hit-testing; square and ink colours come from the theme's board-<role> variables with the dark board as fallback, with a fixed highlight priority (selected, cursor, check, capture, last move, plain).

Each agent run is a Textual worker in the agent-run group streaming astream with stream modes messages and values on the thread captured at submit: values chunks replace the app state, model-node message text accumulates as analysis (a new message id starts it afresh), and afterwards (even on an ordinary exception) the state is reloaded via aget_state, the position packet is cleared once a turn or outcome exists, and running is cleared; an exception records the failure while the turn stays pending.

Start sends a human go message (or the position packet for a custom root) only when nothing is running or pending, the game isn't over, it is the agent's move and no packet is unanswered, and runs automatically at game start when the agent is to move; retry sends an empty payload on the same thread when a turn is pending (or resends a failed first position packet) and does nothing otherwise, so a retried turn commits once.

Human moves are refused with a notice when the game is over or an earlier position is being browsed, with a warning while the agent runs or a turn is pending, and with 'It's the agent's move.' when it isn't the human's turn; the board is interactive only when live and _can_move holds.

Starting a game (_start_game, from New Game or Rematch) cancels the agent-run worker group, starts a _forget worker that waits for the cancelled runs to unwind and then deletes the previous thread's checkpoints with adelete_thread, and creates a new tui-<uuid> thread with reset state; late events and failures from the previous game therefore never reach the new game.

TUI visual regressions are SVG snapshot tests covering board sizes, selection, Black orientation, the promotion dialog, and a hybrid game screen built through build_agent with a FakeRanker and ScriptedModel and the latency clock patched to zero (full, light/narrow, short and stacked layouts, stepping back, game over, New Game, a stopped turn, an invalid Advanced field), updated with pytest --snapshot-update after inspecting the SVGs.
The TUI's widgets render model output, errors and SAN as plain Textual Content and the #note line is a Static with markup disabled, so such text is displayed literally rather than parsed as markup.

The CLI resolves settings from an optional --config versioned settings file (or ChessContext() defaults), then overlay resets each --reset key to its default and applies the given flags before revalidating; unknown reset keys or version raise SettingsError, and any ValueError (bad file, bad --model-kwargs JSON, invalid value) becomes typer.BadParameter with exit code 2.

The opponent label on the player strip (opponent_label) names System 1 and the LLM by preset names and takes the effort from sent(context), so an effort given in model_kwargs shows, with the suffix only when an effort is set.

The game screen adapts to terminal width: 160+ columns is the full three-column layout with Last Reply on the left, 88-159 is the wide layout with Last Reply moved after the table, and under 88 everything stacks vertically and scrolls.

lcchess play --fen starts from a position: start_problem rejects unparsable FENs and positions already over under the game's draw claims (exit code 2 against --fen), and a game from a non-standard root sends a position packet, resent by Retry until a turn accepts it, with the human's first move carried inside the packet.

The New Game screen derives the policy from the System 1 and LLM pickers (only System 1: systemone, only LLM: llm, both: hybrid), forces reasoning_effort off for models that don't take one, holds Play until the matchup is a valid ChessContext, and checks in a background worker whether the LLM has a known input limit before allowing memory.

When a new game picks a different context, the app builds its agent with the factory before dropping the current game; a ValueError or ImportError keeps the current game, notifies the user and reopens New Game with the picks, while an unchanged context reuses the existing agent; a random side is resolved once by a coin flip.

Resign asks for confirmation and sends 'resign <human side>', allowed once the game has started and nothing is running (also after a failed turn); offering a draw sends 'draw <human side>' only on the human's live move and not twice at the same ply; rematch restarts the same game with sides swapped.

Browsing sets a viewed index (None follows the game): the board shows that position and is not interactive, the move input is disabled, arriving moves don't move the view, and the Last Reply panel shows the reply before the viewed move.

The Last Reply panel shows the open pending turn, an in-flight stand-in while a run is out before its turn lands, or the latest agent move, broken into System 1 and LLM stages (or forced) with statuses, recorded latency_ms model times (never wall-clock), costs and a game-so-far summary.

The command palette exports the game: Copy PGN (web-app headers, Site lcchess play, a comment with the opponent, changed knobs and thread id, opening comments), Copy FEN of the shown position, Save PGN to langchain-chess-<thread>.pgn in the current directory, and Analyze on Lichess, which falls back to the shown position when the PGN link would exceed 8000 characters.

Opening names come from the shared Lichess chess-openings table (openings.json links to the web app's file) looked up by position key, so transpositions are named and the latest named position at or before the index holds after leaving the book.

The TUI registers two themes built from the web app's Macaw colours, langchain (dark, the default) and langchain-light, which supply the board and move-source colours; the light squares are kept darker than the web's so white block-art pieces stay visible.
